correctness.rationale: For nonloops i!=j, local dependency Poisson approximation has aggregate O(1) absolute error; loops contribute O(n^(gamma/2)). The divisor summatory expansion and Stieltjes integral yield the n^gamma log n and n^gamma coefficients with O(n^(gamma/2)) remainder. For unordered pairs the adjacent occurrence bound sums to O(n^gamma). A pointwise deletion inequality gives Var(E_n)<=8 E(E_n), hence L2 and almost-sure limits by geometric subsequences. The standard infinite Zipf occupancy law yields the mean degree limits. Standalone enumeration passed 17,939 exact-rational finite checks; these do not establish the analytic steps.

value.rationale: The literature analyzes fixed-degree distributions, leaving the finite-size total edges and average degree quantitatively unresolved. The n^gamma log n regime and explicit second-order n^gamma correction resolve a natural natural-network observable and reveal that the mean degree diverges logarithmically while the published degree tail exponent remains two; merging orientations changes its leading constant nontrivially by 2^(gamma-1). The exact Zipf divisor product makes a reusable method for heavy-tail sequential pattern statistics.
